summary: The note traces the enlargement of the European Union from its predecessor, the European Economic Community, founded with six member states in 1958 when the Treaty of Rome took effect. It states that membership has grown to twenty-eight, with Croatia the latest member to join in July 2013. It also notes the most recent territorial enlargement, Mayotte in 2014, and two notable territorial reductions: Algeria's exit upon independence in 1962 and Greenland's exit in 1985.
one_line: Overview of how the European Union grew from six founding members in 1958 to twenty-eight, plus territorial gains and losses.
key_facts: The EU's predecessor, the European Economic Community, was founded with the Inner Six member states in 1958.
The European Economic Community was founded in 1958, when the Treaty of Rome came into force.
The EU's membership has grown to twenty-eight member states.
The latest member state of the European Union is Croatia, which joined in July 2013.
The most recent territorial enlargement of the European Union was the incorporation of Mayotte in 2014.
The exit of Algeria upon its independence in 1962 was one of the most notable territorial reductions of the European Union and its predecessors.
The exit of Greenland in 1985 was one of the most notable territorial reductions of the European Union and its predecessors.
The European Union's predecessors include the European Economic Community.
